body:
Our National Security depends on people of resolve and dedication speaking out and working to stem the worst of the effects of Trump as he rolls out Project 2025.
#
Peter, we won’t be able to take on every single horrendous thing that comes out of the Trump administration these last two years.
We’re going to need to be focused, and we’re going to need to drill in on righteous fights where we can have an impact.
And, frankly, when we do pick those righteous fights... it’ll still be a tough time to win them. We’re dealing with a man who’s made his intentions clear: A wannabe tyrant.
**But none of this — not a single piece of it — means that we won’t fight back. VoteVets will be on the frontline, same as we always have been.** There is too much at stake to check out and give up. Our National Security depends on people of resolve and dedication speaking out, spreading the word, and working to stem the worst of the effects of Trump.
And today, one of the next fights is taking shape.
**Reporting indicates that one of the core Military goals of Project 2025 — the purge of “disloyal” senior officers and their replacement by loyalists who swear an oath to Trump alone — is coming together.**
Everyone vows to support and defend the Constitution when you join the Military. Most people know this. When you continue in your career, your promotions are determined by fellow officers — and ultimately are approved by the Senate when you reach the senior ranks of Generals or Admirals.
Pete Hegseth is intentionally blocking promotions for more than a dozen senior promotions, unsurprisingly, many of them women and people of color. These are officers who were selected for promotion by a thorough merit-based process and represent the very best of our country.
By withholding their promotion, Trump and Hegseth are effectively forcing many to retire early and end their military service. Once they’re gone, we can expect that Trump will elevate officers who will answer every order he gives without question — legal or otherwise.
**It is outright, clear politicization of the Military over professionalism and competence, and it puts the entire Constitutional order on the chopping block.** Our Military is the most powerful and capable force in the history of the world, and Trump and Hegseth are trying to destroy it. History is littered with defeated militaries who sacrificed their warfighting capability on the altar of politics.
If Trump succeeds, our adversaries will take note, and we will all be less safe.
Peter, we want to make this absolutely clear: We might not be able to prevent Trump and Hegseth from doing incalculable damage to our Military. But you can be damn sure we’re going to try.
[**Please. We need you to add your name and speak out against this blatant attempt to purge and politicize the Military. Our best option today is to come together and speak out against this. Make noise. We have to make it politically untenable.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/General_nov_su_em/?source=em261128-1-misc&refcode2=35820.3013755.zfrn8Q&akid=35820%2E3013755%2Ezfrn8Q)
| [SIGN ON NOW](https://act.votevets.org/signup/General_nov_su_em/?source=em261128-1-misc&refcode2=35820.3013755.zfrn8Q&akid=35820%2E3013755%2Ezfrn8Q)

subject: How is this even legal
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
Right now, members of Congress are allowed to engage in insider trading
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-congress-stock-trading-poll/?refcode=em261128-1-180&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)
Friend — right now, members of Congress are allowed to engage in insider trading, which is illegal for any other person in any other situation.
That’s right, by allowing members of Congress to buy and sell individual stocks, **the law currently allows our representatives to use their power to get incredibly rich** , often making millions and millions of dollars.
Some members use insider knowledge from private or classified briefings to get ahead of the markets. Some members even invest in companies that they are tasked with overseeing on their committees. **_It’s legalized corruption and an astounding conflict of interest._**
Luckily for us, Ilhan Omar leads with integrity. She doesn’t trade stocks and she doesn’t cash in on her access to power. She fights for the advancement of the working class, not her investment portfolio or her bank account.
But, given how common this problem is in Washington, Ilhan is wondering: [**Would you support our new Democratic majorities taking up legislation to finally BAN members of Congress from trading stocks? Vote here:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-congress-stock-trading-poll/?source=em261128-1-180&refcode2=2616.791427.iz7fxq&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)
**[YES](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-congress-stock-trading-poll/?source=em261128-1-180&refcode2=2616.791427.iz7fxq&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)**
**[NO](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-congress-stock-trading-poll/?source=em261128-1-180&refcode2=2616.791427.iz7fxq&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)**
**[I'M NOT SURE](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-congress-stock-trading-poll/?source=em261128-1-180&refcode2=2616.791427.iz7fxq&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)**
When we elect our representatives, they should be working for us. We pay their salaries with our tax dollars after all!
But the current system introduces a conflict between the needs of a member’s constituents and their desire to grow their personal fortune. How can we trust that someone is voting with the country’s best interests in mind, rather than their wallet’s?
It should be a given that Congress is not a get-rich-quick scheme, and it’s a sad reality that some politicians use it as such. It degrades the entire point of public service and representative democracy.
[**If you agree, add your vote to Ilhan Omar’s survey today and make your voice heard. Combating corruption and abuses of power must be priority number one if we want to restore our democracy and make it work for We the People >>**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-congress-stock-trading-poll/?source=em261128-1-180&refcode2=2616.791427.iz7fxq&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)
**[MAKE YOUR VOTE](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-congress-stock-trading-poll/?source=em261128-1-180&refcode2=2616.791427.iz7fxq&akid=2616%2E791427%2Eiz7fxq)**
Thank you in advance for letting us know what you think!
In solidarity,
Team Ilhan

name: Demand Justice PAC
subject: A court just reopened Trump’s escape hatch
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Demand Justice PAC
body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261128-62030&t=1001&akid=62030%2E1407376%2EQ-1x70 ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261128-62030&t=1002&akid=62030%2E1407376%2EQ-1x70 ]Demand Justice PAC

A federal
appeals court gave Donald Trump something a Manhattan jury wouldn't: a
possible way out of his criminal conviction.

Here’s what happened: In 2024, a jury convicted Trump of 34 felonies for
faking business records to bury a $130,000 hush money payment to Stormy
Daniels before the 2016 election.

He's the first president ever convicted of a crime. He served zero days.
And now, he wants the conviction gone.

His lawyers have spent three years trying to drag the case into federal
court, where he can claim "presidential immunity." A federal judge said no
three times.

Now, a federal appeals court is giving Trump another shot. It ordered a
lower court to rule again, fast. If the new ruling goes his way, Trump
gets another chance to wipe out his conviction, and his state appeal could
be frozen while he tries.

The Supreme Court opened this door. In July 2024, its far-right majority
ruled that presidents are immune from prosecution for official acts, and
that those acts can't even be used as evidence to prove other crimes.
Trump's team has used that ruling to attack his conviction ever since.

Hush money isn't an official act. Lying in business records isn't an
official act. But again and again, our courts keep telling Trump the rules
don't apply to him.

A man with 34 felony convictions shouldn't get to shop around until he
finds a court willing to make them disappear. The courts are supposed to
protect the people, not a wannabe authoritarian.

Demand Justice PAC is fighting back. We're exposing every ruling that
bends the law for Trump and making sure Americans know who our courts are
really serving.

This is Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA).
On Election Day, we knocked Jim Crow flat on its back. But if we’re not careful, it’ll rear its ugly head again.
Just look at what we were up against this year:
In April, the Supreme Court struck down Louisiana’s second majority-Black congressional district.
The very next day, Gov. Jeff Landry declared a state of emergency and suspended our congressional primaries, just days before early voting was set to begin and with mail ballots already in voters’ hands.
**_They redrew the lines. They canceled the vote. They did everything short of padlocking the polling places._**
And it didn’t work.
On Nov. 3, Black voters across the Deep South turned out in extraordinary numbers. 93% of Black women voted Democratic. And here in Louisiana’s 5th District, a district drawn to favor Republicans, I finished FIRST.
But I’ve lived long enough to know one thing about Jim Crow: it never stays down on its own.
It changes clothes. It shows up as a new map, a new ID law, a sudden “state of emergency.” And the moment we stop showing up, it gets right back up and rears its ugly head.
That’s what’s at stake on December 12.
If our turnout drops off in this runoff, the same people who canceled our elections will tell the whole country that Nov. 3 was a fluke. But if we win, I’ll become the first Black woman Louisiana has ever sent to Congress, in a district they never expected us to win.
That’s how you keep Jim Crow down. Not with one election. With continued fervor.

Mary Moriarty tried to keep Cam and me apart. The judge said NO.What really happened in the ten minutes inside. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

Patriot,

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABGZtkAlmFvugGcLYY5Roo6hoqrX1H6DNC00wOiN0JcO6OF7GDWXVJA4vKlRs1aFzyqtglgOrx3tciuH20W7EOirsb1EXaSD2QgjcxI8

Standing room only.

I want to take you inside that Minneapolis courtroom on November 16, the day of my first court appearance, because the ten minutes I spent in there told me more about this case than ten weeks of headlines.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABGZtkAlndqQvDJiiBJLVfwbVeoVbdmvbyOnSueT8uEk0k5RHesM1fZohcvXx-Vai9MG8YTgzbOpk-dKefrKXaYDbqqyVNw0zHg1_qZI
Stand with me now.

The room was small, and it was packed. People lined the walls and spilled out the open door into the lobby, and Cam Higby and I had to stand against the very back wall. It looked like the waiting room of a bus depot: reporters on tablets, a few patriots in “Don't Tread on Me” gear, people in wheelchairs, and the families of men in orange jumpsuits waiting behind the glass for their own turn.

A woman standing near us held up her iPhone to record Cam, but she wasn't very good at it, and the whole time we could hear the little record button clicking on and off.

“There is no recording in this courtroom,” the judge said, looking out over the room. Then, to someone else: “Take your hat off.”

I kept my arms folded the entire time, because I wanted everyone in that room to see that I wasn't even touching my phone. When you're known as the guy who records everyone, you learn to be careful about that.

Then the judge looked up from his papers. “Is this the... O'Keefe case?”

Cam and I made our way up to the front of the room together.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzQsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABGZtkAlobxsA9vzWp96gvlLr209j8_uusz9DbCrfEYE_BhpWIqLqhuNuMDdfCiTfNV_G2PT8EVWqv7qeE4-JKe4hpHpQyPiq2DRifLk
Help me keep going.

Here is what I need you to know about those ten minutes, because the prosecution had only one real request that day, and it told me everything. They asked the judge to bar me from talking to Cam.

Think about that for a second. Cam and I work together, we investigate together, and we were charged together for the very same reporting, yet the very first thing the county wanted from that judge was to cut the line of communication between two working journalists.

The judge said NO.

He said he couldn't do that, and he even noted that two men had traveled all the way from other parts of the country to be in his courtroom that day, which he called a good showing.

And the woman who brought these charges? Mary Moriarty still wasn't in the room. She had sent someone else to stand at the table and ask the judge for that order on her behalf.

I don't believe for a moment that request was an accident. Nobody tries to separate two reporters because of something they did back in August; you try to separate them because of what they might do next. Keeping us apart, slowing us down and making every single phone call feel risky is the real goal here.

body:
A few weeks before the election, I cut dahlias from my backyard garden.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261128-6989-footer&t=1&akid=6989%2E420207%2EfS55j_)
Peter,
One of my absolute favorite things to do is spend time in my garden.
A few weeks before the election, I cult the dahlias from my backyard garden. I put in so much work nurturing these wonderful flowers, and that thought made me pause.
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261128.aNF7Rv&refcode=em20261128-6989&t=2&akid=6989%2E420207%2EfS55j_)
I think about it a lot, actually — what it takes to grow something. You can’t rush it. You have to show up, consistently, even when nothing seems to be happening. You water, you tend, and you wait. And then one day, something beautiful blooms that wasn’t there before.
**Growing a garden is a lot like growing a movement. And earlier this November, we saw our movement bloom.**
But it didn’t sprout overnight. It was born out of our collective resistance. It grew from the soil that is our community. Organizing together, showing up, refusing to give in for years, even when the ground felt dry and progress felt slow. We’ve never given up.
30,000+ people trained in nonviolent resistance. Progressive candidates winning races across the country against billions in dark money. A people-powered movement that is strong, determined, and continuing to grow each day.
**That is what sustained, grounded, and committed organizing looks like.** Just like a garden, you don’t just plant the seeds and walk away. You nurture it. You protect it. You come back to it every single day.
We have to keep doing the work. It’s not enough to have won the election. When Democrats take the majority in January, we must keep nurturing this movement and actually deliver what voters expect of us.
I’m going to be pushing my colleagues in Congress to do just that every single day. But I’m counting on your help to keep our movement strong.
[**If you can, will you please pitch in $3, or whatever is meaningful to you, to help us reach our $30,000 end-of-month goal and keep growing this movement?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261128.aNF7Rv&refcode=em20261128-6989&amount=3&t=3&akid=6989%2E420207%2EfS55j_)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

Friends and Neighbors,

Earlier this week I asked a question on Facebook about the way we tax property. I didn’t expect it to reach close to 6 million people. Facebook shows it was shared more than 26,000 times.

That tells me this is a conversation people want to have. I’ve included the post below, along with what I’ve been saying about county budgets and what we heard at three Truth Tour stops. If you’ve got a question or a story about your own tax bill, hit reply. I’d like to hear it.

Ryan Chamberlin

Why this property tax post struck a nerve

Ryan’s Facebook graphic on property taxes and rising home values

Put police, fire and schools first

Umstead State Park and ending near Jackson. The nearly continuous 83-mile path destroyed hundreds of homes and businesses, damaged thousands more, injured over 150 people, and claimed four lives. ## **Outer Banks Flooding Closes Highway 12**
A Thanksgiving nor'easter brought heavy rain, wind, and coastal flooding to the Outer Banks, closing three sections of [N.C. Highway 12](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ8GOq_8wxpTuIgU0d20KdGsPYAVYyN7Lta-fcRKeYKUo9F8853z-2v5ghBD2n7BgXZNbknYakQiLEsJF8Tyboh_9rDtDd5CejhgWySXmgnBpFnOkuuJjhbRezuOSk--RyvG6Wn0wI3pd-s11-alwSvpn69BDprjNGqH43N6jkL1wd5AIaQRghtuHnKVyoOGcUKlNPJu4OgD5fJY4ztfWFIutDsoOYYED5ePPtqd6Kyd-tHJuZNza-3RCsR72cn5jtXJuRIQ3uN9z_4BmMtQidWwpbAGB4nYGnP2IW0s5YJQCQtL-cLjhYXdsvcTNX_TsdT8XRx26qfbgbaTPjbF-rOFGEPVYzfw7YDwMenpf0u-rPwbAAD__87Fk7k) on Friday, including routes on Hatteras and Ocracoke. Crews are assessing damage after the storm breached thousands of feet of dunes and damaged about 375 feet of [pavement between Frisco and Hatteras](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkMuq5CAQQL_G7Axa5mEWLgaG7Hq2sww1WklkTAxqt_TfX9LcP7i7ggOn6tTfx_JAH_y5_cGDzHra5aSaA5VCaUn-hSG9K9H_3W97xbcEhwduCwgYuJQc9HKlmC-yZZGNM-Oohsk1ZOQ49XrohNbNbrTTK4D8NynUoBG7XmMPTnRqpKnvoPHmFkoJWkqhhW5hBeVwwHEipQYSrBPkfImpXcM7viidMZXdYorBn9jaeDTB7KVcmalfDGYGc621rb6cN2Qw3wsYzFLe88hgvjCVzL-7uASe6EB_chtiJsdtopo55kw580803V41P8ux5PhMlpj6bXcs21U-ByTjrupD8HkYWSe2A334gPLTv74MfAUAAP__SniMMQ). A section of Avon Fishing Pier washed out in the storm, marking its second storm-related damage in about two months; the latest damage was described as minor compared with September's.
## Rivalries Shape Playoff and Bowl Hopes

## Donors Keep Radford Dancers in Parade
Eight Radford dancers will be able to perform in today's rescheduled Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade after supporters raised [about $4,000](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2unjAURFdjOiN8_QeFizR0L21KdLEv4MgYZBzQt_uI6O0g3UgjHc2ZX1_TF8YU8_oTd3L1XqZMz5WoVipTwbAcJQTMnsq1Y_HbkT3eOEEHhgvBoZ_Q13jTpLAJbkFFODTkhB10b5RUfbM5YcOyoJIEg5Z-luj1bMxiJVrVa2Ob6F6eENALIQB0K8UgQYtOazPjbIipjkKsR2nrRncsa8wRl_Q5biqtP_Ymua3W82LyB4ORwfg8T_uE-bd9Wwbjy2cwCvFmy2Dc0X8ufmLBQDxQwg-vWyGslCnwb3H-bc7nuPL92ClXXjfKfKN08vP4UygwGJviwvnElOJlLFPdumNM_2bV_3z0dvA3AAD__769iwY) toward added costs. Hotel extensions initially ran about $300 per performer, with more donations going toward transportation and food. New York City officials, the NYPD and Macy's moved the parade from Thursday to Saturday, its [first-ever postponement](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb_GdKzssWGhcPGkJ7pNE0Up0WAPMArYyHZY8ffR5hdSX-nqnPP5GB_IG4flDXey5ZzHQM-8USmUxoR-jsl7DI5S3jG5NQaHJ44goa2VqqEb0RU-aTRYeTujIewrsureN11rtOmq1U4efA_aSd_LSWlC37qpxztJjX0DqmL7-lMKOqUUQHPTqtfQKNk07YRTS8JI8lxiupWVTk4LB8Z5u-JJ6ebiXm12LeXIQv8TMAgYcHIvj9cmYPh4FzDs6K5clxXDV1745LDUHq_6wISe6iPmcsRAvs7xOznKAoZcYrqEHtgL_V_pzjRgpKqS9ceTt41zexdGLjvy9gtR_tjvtPATAAD__031hVQ) in the event's 100-year history. Most families had planned to leave Friday, and weekend train tickets were largely sold out. The Derek Wagner Dance Center students will perform alongside [600 dancers with Spirit](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE9jMiN3YxgIHGxCNptuiBq7gd7lT8YymtuvZjQ3-LKSSnqqV3-ew5NklX3-TRu7lKdh5_taOSWOQ6QwHTEE2j3Ha6Pol2P3lGlAg40G0NgO5JNkHiwVwU1kmbqCHTy6um1sZdticTZAW5uqGtuOOg81jN5w583UWQje-kLcmweALQAg1mUFXYU1mLpuRhobVtZwkHTEMi2cJc6yC03r68gcS39sxeqWlM5LVb8U9gr7-77LO4x_H-9WYf_mK-wBPllhzzIvSX_N9FdUnxynI24ajEmL3si_Lp0W2v9ds2TZZx3opU-KFFhhX0QXzlvWVa7moayZN5L1Myf98Mns8H8AAAD__wEjh3s) of America. Heather Smith said her daughter Erica, who graduated in May, is capping her dance career with the parade. Smith said the support feels "like a million bucks."
## Cavaliers Aim To End Blacksburg Drought
Virginia visits Virginia Tech today with a chance to keep the Commonwealth Cup and earn its [first win in Blacksburg](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhTAQRE9jOiN2wWAKF2noftqUaDELWDH2l22BcvvoR0oukHpGTzPv4zE_yHkX9nc62ZRrmwPf2XMpnOZE6xbTulKwnPJJyR4xWLpoxgZ7CSBRz2SLu3juqFrNRh3TWLGBYVS679pOV4exxGhB6W4BGGxPShM0lvSgUDWqVZUzLx4AagBAVHULY4sKGqX6hZaeRdfw6kpMdTn4cml3wdHmv-LFqbbxrLw5Snlm0b4JnARO933Xdsn5GVPJr4bAyUbveWe5xVgW8l7g9PoqcPolysz8meXmUi7ydkFSkX9ZYXvI7IJlCeOoBU5VMuvzdt673A-ia_aTnP-ZU_5p8jL4HQAA__-O8Imb) since 1998. Most families had planned to leave Friday, and weekend train tickets were largely sold out. The Derek Wagner Dance Center students will perform alongside of America. Heather Smith said her daughter Erica, who graduated in May, is capping her dance career with the parade. Smith said the support feels "like a million bucks." Cavaliers Aim To End Blacksburg Drought Virginia visits Virginia Tech today with a chance to keep the Commonwealth Cup and earn its since 1998. The Cavaliers reclaimed the trophy last year with a 27-7 win in Charlottesville. Virginia trailed 29-7 at halftime in that 1998 game before rallying to win 36-32, the in school history. The Cavaliers are still looking for their first win away from Charlottesville this season, while the Hokies will and look to end a three-game skid. Kroger Begins Corporate Layoffs Cincinnati-based Kroger began to corporate employees just before Thanksgiving as part of a plan to eliminate about 3,000 corporate positions by 2029. ## Hackers Breach Air Force Cloud Network
Hackers broke into Cloud One, the Air Force's [flagship cloud computing](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAUhE9jOiP8g2ELF2noNm1KZB7P-CUGI-MF5fYRe4V0I430ab75eo5PR5G25dOtaItP44bXEbEUzKOj7FMGDA5-cIYUIy6Y6XSjbKThQnDZjw4KnTiKarYeUaKq0Iru0fam1bqvgp1AON13k-_7VssWjNKdUAA4twYVQkX2xgkheyFUo9taeSMfqnm0TgjfGcN0gzOVlOvvRFsJ6ONvOjHXkNYq2lDKfjD1weTA5HBdVw3bBHfJ5HCjmRyEuHPH5PCWyQefMjoI_HVwR5m_PbmPbjkC7Rxies08bcghrfur0LbwPbriU17rUNZYZTvvF8VIh-mYbpbVUXzvKf978bTyLwAA__-PwoZ-) platform, in an intrusion discovered within the past month during a system upgrade, three people familiar with the matter told reporters Friday. The intruders exploited an unidentified software flaw to reach the control plane, the layer that manages the entire platform. Cyber Command has been [called in to assess](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwRsRXGM-BoYu3tK1o0XgEt-WmAhTR3n7KnmFzkf6S7_zdV7OgQpt189wQ99zXTZ87AV7x7YEarm2iGuIP5hiLQWv2OgICwjQXEoOdgmx04GLHJLPiIDjgF4aN1k9KWWH1WPEYEeX7CVDVgIVigsaFZwzLpjJDuRfOSnBSjkKNZ3GrMGNwk1Bymy0Zkpgol7b6bvS1lfM5VkPbKdYb0Pxa-_3nY0fDGYGc19xpVJeG4P5XgvFJ4M5YcZtRwazBjVJZ3igxt88Hkv9TbxuyF9SBvPQfLo_qBTatWFKXG-B3sWh_--jw8NfAAAA___4xXoS) the damage, one source said. Cloud One runs Defense Department applications covering personnel, pay, logistics, and maintenance, including a command and control system that collects air defense radar feeds from across North America and a program that tracks bombs and missiles. The Air Force said it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems." The breach follows reported intrusions this month at the [FBI, CIA, and Treasury](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGunTAQRVdjOiNswEDhIg3dT5sSDfYYnAwYmQH0dh_995bw-6urc86fr-kLIsV9-Q0bWg5p2vE5CZkxTxBzSNnhCu4fepeIcMEcb5h0pY1USup-AsfxxkkV3gZEjXWBVnVD25u2afpite2sgzGtgab3qh3mrvN-AO97p0LV1VBE-32nlO6VqqumLetg9FBXQwtKhc4Y0VToI6dc_k1x5xUDvdKNuXRpK8iuzMcp6l9Cj0KPz_OUMyEecV9c2o6LP0Ohx281occT3ZUjv4Qer1NCzPJtKR2ly8uDgEPKm8x4pMzo6SU_AWTcJQHjyTKgxwwk54zgVqHHIlt_PJEonqYTTbVsEOnNxz-relv9PwAA__-Gx48n) Department.
## FCC Clears 1 Million SpaceX Satellites
The Federal Communications Commission [cleared SpaceX to deploy](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhTAUg58mbEH5JwwZurDdrh3RaXJySRsIChG0b19xX6GbJVu2_H085geknLbnO6zoWizzhteRsTWsM6QaS_W4gP_G4EvO-MSaTpgFE4ZyToWdwbd04sy74CKiQNmh48OordFK2W5xKmhrg5fD4C0PwjBludZ-GK0cR8ugS-6u41xYziVTupfRiFGyUQPncTCGKIYhtVL7r5K2tmDMv-XE2vuydtktre0HkW9ETERM13X1_vO4b9w-EdMtiZiOHTz-0Og9hX2v5YRMAzSgHreG9aCvABFTV13Yr5RzOsxAFHuukPJrq_2P0OnEXwAAAP__r6F6Gw) up to 1 million satellites that would operate as data centers in orbit, the first authorization of its kind in U.S. history. The network, called Starmind, would run artificial intelligence work on solar-powered [orbital compute modules](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhTAQBNDTmA7kXWwDhYs0dD9tSrTfrD9ODEbGguT2EblCupFGeiPNx2N6UIhhe73Tyrb4NG18HZFL4TxRyD5lxwu5L55dipFfnMNJE0o0NUCN_USuhJMnqGbrmZHbii10g-6NVqqvFqtbhU9DWndyeILv5KCMUcq5mbCX0FbB3hwA9gCtVLppvcGhlYMmAN8ZI5TkOZSUm88UtrKwjz_p5Ny4tFbRLqXsh2jfBI4Cx-u6Grc93V0KHG9a4AhwZy1wPHZy_F175-qDCscYCte07zmdFJulrLHKdt6vEGM4TCeUfK0U4t9W-d9Dp8XfAAAA__9qBHfz), which SpaceX says use energy more efficiently than data centers on the ground. The grant [comes with limits](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU9jMiNXAQYCB5uQ9aYbompTBu8a3LK9MDOnH9FXmPg__Se9P4_5QT74Y_1NO5vi4nzwlQOXwmkmn1xMljey_3ixMQReOfmTZlSoJYDEYSZb_MkzVItxzMhNxQb6sRt017ZDtZnuiURP7ngg7kErp6nRvaYnDTCyGytv7jsAHAAa1XZ14zSOjRo7AnC91qJVvPgSU_03-qNs7MJnPDnVNu5VMFspryyaXwIngdN1XfVBmfKLLLvg163cnMDptgicAAROzlpJ_8sWk__iLN_whwS5-xB8PGQulHZ_LBJVqwROVTLL67rHrHvRqnUnH97-8rNqp8HvAAAA___8A4CQ). SpaceX can fly between roughly 310 and 620 miles up, nothing above 373 miles until regulators approve its debris plan, and the first satellite must be working by November 2033. Amazon, Viasat, and astronomers objected, [citing orbital debris](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQAL_GdCDv2mAoXLyG7l6bEvnM-tjEYGRbXO7vo8svpB5pNJqP23JzHPl4_Hc72RrSctCzRKqV8uI4h5Q9bc5_0epTjPSgzJdbUOLQArQ4Ls5XvmiBZrWBCEk1ZMFM_Tj0Wo_NZu9hQq3wriBoBWoccZzQGO3NigBmati-dQA4Aiip-06FASclp94BBDMMQktauabcfSY-6kYhvtJFufNpb6Ldaj2LUP8EzgLnSn7rXm5L6Y0FzsUzHZ4Ezi5X9pGKwDl43_p0rFw5HS7GV-vOM6eLSltO5-m7PaM7WuhBSjkY6La6xybb9XxyjFwGI7R87I7jb0T927rL4k8AAAD__2-2gfU) and harm to telescopes. The launches still need Federal Aviation Administration approval. Musk wrote on X that the system will be "a great asset to America and the world."

The intruders exploited an unidentified software flaw to reach the control plane, the layer that manages the entire platform. Cyber Command has been the damage, one source said. Cloud One runs Defense Department applications covering personnel, pay, logistics, and maintenance, including a command and control system that collects air defense radar feeds from across North America and a program that tracks bombs and missiles. The Air Force said it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems." The breach follows reported intrusions this month at the Department. clean_body: The Pride of Pearland Marching Band to keep its 500 members in New York City after a storm forced the first postponement in Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade history. | | | | | | Saturday, November 28, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning! On this day in 1835, left Mexico City, leading a force of approximately 6,000 soldiers on a challenging winter campaign spanning 900 to 1,000 miles north into Texas. Today's edition is a little shorter as our team spends Thanksgiving weekend with family and friends. We hope you're enjoying some good company, a little downtime, and maybe one more slice of pie. We'll be back with the full edition on Monday. Christmas lists don't check themselves. The 2026 Flyover Gift Guide is here, and Amy Hess is unwrapping some of our favorites on The Flyover Podcast. From stocking stuffers to big-ticket surprises, and a few gifts you may not have even thought of. Consider your list handled. ! If you look forward to our "On This Day" stories, today's sponsor, the , is offering 30% off Texas history books, historic maps, and signed Texas art at Legacy of Texas with code through Cyber Monday. Abilene ☀️ 74°/44° | Amarillo 🌤️ 70°/30° | Austin ☀️ 74°/56° | Brownsville 🌤️ 77°/63° | Corpus Christi 🌤️ 78°/59° | DFW ☀️ 71°/51° | El Paso 🌤️ 77°/46° | Houston 🌤️ 74°/63° | Laredo ☀️ 82°/55° | Lubbock 🌤️ 72°/37° | Midland ☀️ 77°/40° | San Antonio ☀️ 73°/54° | Tyler ☀️ 71°/53° | Waco ☀️ 72°/53° | Texas Rallies to Keep Performers in NYC The Pride of Pearland Marching Band to keep its 500 members in New York City after a storm forced the first postponement in Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade history. With the 100th edition moved from Thursday to Saturday, more than 1,900 donors chipped in, including H-E-B, CenterPoint Energy, and Houston's Mattress Mack. The money covers , meals, and charter buses home Saturday, since flights are booked into next week. Band director Ryan Demkovich called the support humbling. Other Texas groups face the same squeeze. North Texas' set a $50,000 goal to cover extra hotel nights and Sunday flights for 55 dancers, while flight changes and some hotel costs for its Central Texas dance team. Highway Debris Shreds Tires in Denton Debris scattered across northbound Interstate 35E in Denton on Thanksgiving night sparked to police dispatch as drivers pulled over with damaged tires. Police off at Fort Worth Drive as crews cleared the road, after a tow truck driver flagged possible scattered screws. Crews later found that police say likely caused the damage and doesn't appear to have been placed intentionally. You've probably seen the buzz about Elon Musk and SpaceX gifting shares to American children via Trump Accounts. Is this for real? Should you open a Trump Account for the kids in your lives?
The answers are yes and yes. You should.
Let me speak to this personally. I have two children and have now opened Trump Accounts for them. SpaceX shares are worth $131 each as of this writing. Each child gets 2 shares, 1 from SpaceX and 1 from Elon. That's $262 each, and since I have 2 children, that's $524. Elon has said that he's going to do this every year as well, which would be another $262 a year, assuming the share price stays the same. The money becomes accessible at age 18.
Elon's commitment is for approximately $9 billion a year, which would be the single biggest individual voluntary wealth transfer from an individual to other individuals in history. Undertaken over multiple years, it's an enormous deal.
My kids are too old to benefit from the free $1,000 that goes to any child born between Jan. 1st, 2025 (so any 1-year-olds essentially) and Dec. 31st, 2028 for Trump Accounts. And we also don't benefit from the Michael and Susan Dell $250 each for children born between 2016 and 2024 in ZIP codes with a median income of $150k or less. But a lot of kids would obviously qualify for one or both of these.
These are billions of dollars that are being gifted to any American child for when they turn 18.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83111249-1502-4eb1-9ce3-ce11e3b48135?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Some might be turned off by the name "Trump Accounts" or maybe by Elon and some of his actions or statements.
My message to you is, "That's dumb. Get over it." Your child or infant doesn't know squat about either of these individuals. What they will know is that there's a stash of money that's been put aside for them that will serve them well in life. Multiple shares of SpaceX could be worth a lot a number of years from now. So could $1,000 invested in the S&P 500 in 17 years. My bet is that Trump Accounts will be renamed in 2029 anyway to something more generic, like "Invest for the Future Accounts."
By the way, I have a separate 529 account for each of my children, so I've been squirreling money away for their educations for years. However, no one has been sending free money to these accounts. So I went ahead and opened Trump Accounts for them too.
Have I convinced you? If you're not a parent, maybe you're an uncle or aunt. But if you've got a kid in your life, head to https://trumpaccounts.gov/ today and sign up. They'll thank you later.
It's not every day that people try to send your kids money. Take it.
To check out Forward in your area, click [here](https://substack.com/redirect/492861dd-7420-4871-b3b7-30b9f1a3b503?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It will save you money and time - hundreds of dollars for the average American. Look up and be glad for what you have.

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Maintaining America’s Growth Mindset
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/midterms-12855599?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Over the past decade, the American economy has grown by around 2.5 percent a year, and output per person has risen faster here than in any other G7 country. Europe, meanwhile, has stagnated: since 2000 the EU has managed less than half America's rate of growth. **As recently as 2008, the European Union's economy was slightly larger than America's. Today the US economy is around 40 percent bigger.** Why? It is not as if the laws of physics are different on this side of the Atlantic, or that there is something special in the air or the water. The difference is that America has pro-growth policies.
---
|
---
| **Don’t be more like Europe** With fifty states trying different approaches side by side, the US has systems competition. Europe, meanwhile, is run from the top down by the European Union in Brussels. Even those parts of Europe that have escaped the terminal embrace of the EU, such as my own native Britain, have been unable to escape the anti-growth mindset destroying Europe. Nothing illustrates it better than the saga of Heathrow, London’s main airport. Heathrow was once one of the busiest airports in the world. But it has only two runways, and the third will not open until 2039 at the earliest. That is more than three decades after the idea was first proposed. **When Heathrow eventually gets its new runway, it will be 38 years since Britain last built a full-length runway anywhere.** Compare that with what is happening next door in Louisiana, where in August SpaceX announced plans for Starbase Louisiana, a $100 billion investment on the Gulf coast with ten launch pads. Construction starts next year, and the first Starship is due to launch by 2029 — a full decade before anything takes off from one extra strip of tarmac in west London. **Why do I mention all this? Because I worry that the same anti-growth mindset that is reducing Britain and Europe to basket case status could take hold in America.** In the recent midterms, more than 700 candidates ran digital ads about data centers, and of the 685 campaigns whose ads took a clear stance, 636 cast them in a negative light or called for more regulation. **As things stand, candidates have little reason to stick their necks out for data centers, and opportunists have every reason to play Huey Long.** Look at what that kind of politics has done to Europe and you can see why the risk to American prosperity is real. Part of the problem is that the benefits of a new data center or power plant are spread across millions of Americans in ways that are real but rarely noticed, while the costs of having one built down the road are obvious and immediate to the people who live nearby. If we want to keep building, we need to make sure that those who live closest to growth share in its rewards. Data centers generate a great deal of tax revenue. **Amazon's data centers in Madison County are projected to bring the Canton Public School District about $22 million a year, Madison County Schools around $8.5 million a year (rising later to $12.5 million), and the county itself roughly $30 million a year in additional revenue.** The question is where that money goes. If it simply funds a bigger local government, residents will see more bureaucracy and little else; if it goes toward lower property taxes, every homeowner in the county has a reason to welcome the next project rather than fight it. Mississippi has every reason to keep backing growth. Not so long ago, a great many people wrote this state off. Today, output per person here has overtaken Britain's (something I could scarcely have imagined during my years in Parliament), we build more cars per person than Germany, and around $79 billion has been invested in the state since 2020. We have gathered the evidence together at MississippiWins.com, where you can look up how your own county is doing or see how Mississippi compares with any state or country. I suspect you will be pleasantly surprised.

Europe, meanwhile, is run from the top down by the European Union in Brussels. Even those parts of Europe that have escaped the terminal embrace of the EU, such as my own native Britain, have been unable to escape the anti-growth mindset destroying Europe. Nothing illustrates it better than the saga of Heathrow, London’s main airport. Heathrow was once one of the busiest airports in the world. But it has only two runways, and the third will not open until 2039 at the earliest. That is more than three decades after the idea was first proposed. When Heathrow eventually gets its new runway, it will be 38 years since Britain last built a full-length runway anywhere. Compare that with what is happening next door in Louisiana, where in August SpaceX announced plans for Starbase Louisiana, a $100 billion investment on the Gulf coast with ten launch pads. This Black Friday weekend, Americans are searching for bargains on televisions, appliances, electronics, and holiday gifts. Retailers are advertising discounts of 20%, 30%, and even 50%.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..VwTy0ZnQZdNzdYNTPA3KqWnPBwWkF4_2AAb7lan-dPQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=225926584)

But what about the one expense Americans cannot afford to ignore--healthcare?
**The biggest savings American families need aren 't at the mall. They're in their healthcare bills, insurance premiums, prescription costs, and medical deductibles.**
_During my campaign for Congress and throughout my career as a physician, I heard the same frustrations repeatedly: healthcare is too expensive, insurance is too complicated, and patients have too little control over their medical decisions._
Patients are frustrated by their inability to speak directly with their doctors, obtain timely appointments, secure approval for necessary medications, and receive recommended treatments without navigating a maze of insurance company requirements.
We spend enormous amounts of money on healthcare, yet the people paying for it and providing it often have the least influence over how the system operates.
**The problem isn 't simply the cost of healthcare. It's who controls the system.**
## Patients and Physicians Have Lost Their Power
Patients are supposed to be the beneficiaries of our healthcare system. Instead, they have become virtually powerless consumers.
Most Americans receive health insurance through their employers, government programs, or individual policies. **Yet they have little control over the cost of their premiums, the extent of their coverage, or which physicians participate in their plans.**
Even those purchasing insurance through the healthcare marketplaces face limited choices, restrictive networks, high deductibles, and coverage limitations. These marketplaces often lack the competition and consumer control we would expect in a truly open market.
When an insurance company denies a medication or procedure, patients must navigate an administrative appeals process that can take weeks or months. In the meantime, their illnesses do not wait.
Physicians are equally frustrated.
Independent medical practices, once the backbone of American medicine, are increasingly being absorbed by large hospital systems, corporate medical groups, and private equity-owned organizations. The remaining ones are unicorns.
Many physicians have become employees whose compensation depends on productivity quotas, patient volume, and financial targets established by their employers. They face stagnant or declining reimbursement, increasing administrative responsibilities, and pressure to generate revenue for their institutions.
**Doctors are increasingly treated like production workers in a healthcare factory rather than independent professionals entrusted with their patients ' lives.**
This creates a fundamental conflict. Physicians take an oath to place their patients' welfare first, but their employers may prioritize revenue, efficiency, and profitability.
At the same time, insurance companies impose prior authorization requirements, restrictive formularies, and claims denials that interfere with the physician-patient relationship.
Insurance companies frequently argue that denying payment does not prevent a physician from providing treatment. Technically, patients can pay for the care themselves and fight for reimbursement afterward.
But we all know the reality. When a patient cannot afford a procedure or medication without insurance coverage, **denying payment effectively means denying access to care.**
The current system gives insurance companies enormous influence over medical decisions without always exposing them to the same consequences experienced by patients when necessary care is delayed or denied.
The result is a healthcare system in which insurance companies, hospital systems, and pharmaceutical corporations wield tremendous economic power, while patients and physicians have comparatively little.
That imbalance needs to change.
## Five Ways to Deliver Real Healthcare Savings
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e2d57511-da7d-469b-b00a-1be2269a3f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The solution begins by restoring economic and professional power to the people who matter most: patients and their physicians.
### 1\. Give Patients Collective Purchasing Power
One of the greatest weaknesses of our current insurance system is that individual patients have almost no negotiating leverage.
_**We should encourage organizational health insurance purchasing arrangements in which members of professional associations, civic organizations, and other qualifying groups can join together to purchase coverage, subject to applicable insurance laws.**_
By combining thousands of members, these organizations could negotiate more competitive premiums, broader physician networks, lower deductibles, and better coverage.
They could also negotiate with smaller insurance companies seeking to compete with dominant carriers in their markets.
Most importantly, these organizations could become powerful patient advocates.
If an insurance company repeatedly denies legitimate claims, imposes unreasonable restrictions, or fails to provide adequate service, the purchasing organization could demand changes--or take its members' business elsewhere.
**Insurance companies should have to compete for patients rather than patients having to fight insurance companies.**
### 2\. Expand Patient-Owned Health Insurance
_**Another approach is to encourage "mutual" health insurance companies owned by their policyholders instead of outside shareholders.**_
Investor-owned insurance companies have financial obligations to their shareholders. While profitability is necessary for any sustainable business, those interests do not always align with the needs of patients.
Mutual insurance companies offer an alternative ownership model in which policyholders can have a voice in governance and hold management accountable.
Patients could exert greater influence over coverage decisions, administrative costs, and negotiations with healthcare providers.
The objective is simple: insurance companies should be financially successful because they provide affordable, effective healthcare coverage--not because they make it unnecessarily difficult to obtain care.
### 3\. Restore Physicians' Bargaining Power
Physicians need greater negotiating power to counterbalance the influence of large insurance companies and hospital systems.
Federal antitrust laws generally restrict independent physicians from collectively negotiating reimbursement rates and contractual terms with insurers unless they meet specific legal requirements.
Congress should reconsider these restrictions and explore reforms that permit appropriate collective negotiations while protecting patients against anticompetitive practices and excessive costs.
States may also have opportunities to establish carefully supervised negotiation arrangements consistent with federal antitrust law.
Physicians should have the ability to negotiate fair compensation, reduce unnecessary administrative burdens, and challenge unreasonable prior authorization requirements.
The goal is not simply higher physician reimbursement. It is to give doctors the professional influence necessary to provide appropriate care without interference from unnecessary financial and administrative obstacles.
### 4\. Protect Physicians' Professional Independence
Physicians employed by hospitals and large medical organizations should have meaningful protections when advocating for their patients.
_**Where legally permitted, employed physicians can organize and engage in collective bargaining to negotiate compensation, working conditions, staffing, productivity requirements, and professional independence.**_
A physician should not fear retaliation or termination for recommending medically appropriate care that conflicts with an employer's financial priorities.
Restoring physician independence is essential to restoring the physician-patient relationship.
**Doctors should answer first to their patients and their professional obligations --not corporate productivity targets.**
### 5\. Hold Insurance Companies Accountable for Unreasonable Denials
Insurance companies must face meaningful consequences when they improperly deny or delay medically necessary care.
Prior authorization can serve a legitimate purpose in managing costs and preventing unnecessary treatment. But it should never become a bureaucratic obstacle designed primarily to discourage patients from receiving necessary care.
Patients deserve timely decisions, transparent medical necessity standards, meaningful appeals, and independent review.
When insurers repeatedly engage in improper denials or unreasonable delays, there should be real financial and regulatory consequences.
Insurance companies should not be rewarded for avoiding legitimate medical expenses at the expense of patient health.
**The financial incentive should be to deliver better healthcare efficiently, not simply to deny payment.**
## The Next Challenge: Reducing Government Healthcare Bureaucracy
Restoring power to patients and physicians is only the first step.
The second step must be to confront the enormous government healthcare bureaucracy that increases administrative costs, creates duplicative requirements, and diverts resources away from patient care. This was a central theme of my campaign.
Government regulations, reporting requirements, and complicated reimbursement systems impose substantial administrative burdens on hospitals, physicians, and healthcare providers.
Some regulations are necessary to protect patients and ensure accountability. Others add costs without providing corresponding improvements in care.
We need to distinguish between the two and eliminate unnecessary bureaucracy wherever possible.
That subject deserves a separate discussion.
## This Black Friday Weekend, Let's Talk About Real Savings
A television discounted by $200 may seem like a great Black Friday deal. But imagine a healthcare system in which a family could save hundreds of dollars each month on insurance premiums, pay less for prescription medications, face lower deductibles, and avoid unnecessary medical expenses.
Those savings could amount to thousands of dollars every year--money families could use for groceries, housing, education, retirement, or simply improving their quality of life.
Unlike a Black Friday sale that lasts only a weekend, affordable healthcare delivers savings throughout the year.
Healthcare companies deserve the opportunity to operate profitable businesses. Hospitals must remain financially sustainable, pharmaceutical companies should be rewarded for innovation, and insurers have a legitimate responsibility to manage costs.
But profitability should result from delivering value, improving outcomes, and operating efficiently--not from unnecessary administrative obstacles, unjustified coverage denials, or limiting access to medically necessary treatment.
**Patients deserve affordable care. Physicians deserve the freedom to practice medicine. And insurance companies must be accountable to the people they insure.**
Healthcare reform cannot succeed unless we address the fundamental imbalance of power that has allowed insurance companies and large healthcare institutions to dominate decisions affecting patients and physicians.
This Black Friday weekend, as Americans search for discounts and bargains, we should remember that the greatest opportunity for meaningful household savings may not be found in a store or online shopping cart.
It may be found in restoring competition, accountability, and patient choice to American healthcare.
**The greatest healthcare bargain isn 't a discount on care. It's a healthcare system that delivers better care at a price Americans can afford.**
_Dr. Michael Goldstein is a physician, attorney, and former Republican candidate for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District._

Mutual insurance companies offer an alternative ownership model in which policyholders can have a voice in governance and hold management accountable. Patients could exert greater influence over coverage decisions, administrative costs, and negotiations with healthcare providers. The objective is simple: insurance companies should be financially successful because they provide affordable, effective healthcare coverage--not because they make it unnecessarily difficult to obtain care. 3\. Restore Physicians' Bargaining Power Physicians need greater negotiating power to counterbalance the influence of large insurance companies and hospital systems. Federal antitrust laws generally restrict independent physicians from collectively negotiating reimbursement rates and contractual terms with insurers unless they meet specific legal requirements. Congress should reconsider these restrictions and explore reforms that permit appropriate collective negotiations while protecting patients against anticompetitive practices and excessive costs. States may also have opportunities to establish carefully supervised negotiation arrangements consistent with federal antitrust law. Physicians should have the ability to negotiate fair compensation, reduce unnecessary administrative burdens, and challenge unreasonable prior authorization requirements. The goal is not simply higher physician reimbursement. It is to give doctors the professional influence necessary to provide appropriate care without interference from unnecessary financial and administrative obstacles. 4\. Protect Physicians' Professional Independence Physicians employed by hospitals and large medical organizations should have meaningful protections when advocating for their patients. Where legally permitted, employed physicians can organize and engage in collective bargaining to negotiate compensation, working conditions, staffing, productivity requirements, and professional independence. A physician should not fear retaliation or termination for recommending medically appropriate care that conflicts with an employer's financial priorities. Restoring physician independence is essential to restoring the physician-patient relationship. Doctors should answer first to their patients and their professional obligations --not corporate productivity targets. 5\. Hold Insurance Companies Accountable for Unreasonable Denials Insurance companies must face meaningful consequences when they improperly deny or delay medically necessary care. Prior authorization can serve a legitimate purpose in managing costs and preventing unnecessary treatment. But it should never become a bureaucratic obstacle designed primarily to discourage patients from receiving necessary care. Patients deserve timely decisions, transparent medical necessity standards, meaningful appeals, and independent review. When insurers repeatedly engage in improper denials or unreasonable delays, there should be real financial and regulatory consequences. Insurance companies should not be rewarded for avoiding legitimate medical expenses at the expense of patient health. The financial incentive should be to deliver better healthcare efficiently, not simply to deny payment. The Next Challenge: Reducing Government Healthcare Bureaucracy Restoring power to patients and physicians is only the first step. The second step must be to confront the enormous government healthcare bureaucracy that increases administrative costs, creates duplicative requirements, and diverts resources away from patient care. This was a central theme of my campaign. Government regulations, reporting requirements, and complicated reimbursement systems impose substantial administrative burdens on hospitals, physicians, and healthcare providers. Some regulations are necessary to protect patients and ensure accountability. Others add costs without providing corresponding improvements in care. We need to distinguish between the two and eliminate unnecessary bureaucracy wherever possible. That subject deserves a separate discussion. This Black Friday Weekend, Let's Talk About Real Savings A television discounted by $200 may seem like a great Black Friday deal. But imagine a healthcare system in which a family could save hundreds of dollars each month on insurance premiums, pay less for prescription medications, face lower deductibles, and avoid unnecessary medical expenses. Those savings could amount to thousands of dollars every year--money families could use for groceries, housing, education, retirement, or simply improving their quality of life. Unlike a Black Friday sale that lasts only a weekend, affordable healthcare delivers savings throughout the year. Healthcare companies deserve the opportunity to operate profitable businesses. Hospitals must remain financially sustainable, pharmaceutical companies should be rewarded for innovation, and insurers have a legitimate responsibility to manage costs. But profitability should result from delivering value, improving outcomes, and operating efficiently--not from unnecessary administrative obstacles, unjustified coverage denials, or limiting access to medically necessary treatment. Patients deserve affordable care. Physicians deserve the freedom to practice medicine. And insurance companies must be accountable to the people they insure. Healthcare reform cannot succeed unless we address the fundamental imbalance of power that has allowed insurance companies and large healthcare institutions to dominate decisions affecting patients and physicians. This Black Friday weekend, as Americans search for discounts and bargains, we should remember that the greatest opportunity for meaningful household savings may not be found in a store or online shopping cart. It may be found in restoring competition, accountability, and patient choice to American healthcare. The greatest healthcare bargain isn 't a discount on care. It's a healthcare system that delivers better care at a price Americans can afford.** Dr. Michael Goldstein is a physician, attorney, and former Republican candidate for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District. Begin with the verdict, because it is the rarest thing in the entire China file: **proof**. In a federal courtroom in Brooklyn, after a trial that ran nearly three months, a jury of Americans weighed twelve counts against Huawei and three affiliates -- **racketeering conspiracy, bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations, conspiring to steal American trade secrets, obstructing justice**. Guilty on ten. Two counts did not stick; everything else did. Prosecutors drew a twenty-year arc, from 2000 to 2020: router source code lifted, robotics technology copied, employees paid bounties for competitors' confidential information, banks deceived about business in Iran, investigators obstructed. Not a hunch. Not an estimate. A verdict, signed by a foreman.
Now place that verdict in its week. Deliberations opened in Brooklyn just as the President flew to Shenzhen for the APEC trilateral -- seated beside Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in the defendants' hometown while an eight-year case against the flagship of Chinese techno-industrial policy came to its end in New York. The jury read counts in the same hours the man who sets our China policy shook hands in Shenzhen. That is the backdrop. Now read what the same government did in the same fortnight -- because this is the case that America sold itself out, and the direction of the sale matters.

body:
January 8, 2011, was a brisk Saturday morning in Tucson, when Congresswoman Gabby Giffords arrived for her “Congress on your Corner” event. I was serving as her district director.
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261128-1-b&t=1&akid=12108%2E3935704%2EvfL8zD)
---
Friends,
My name is Ron Barber, and in 2011, I almost died alongside Gabby Giffords.
January 8, 2011, was a brisk Saturday morning in Tucson, when Congresswoman Gabby Giffords arrived for her “Congress on your Corner” event. I was serving as her district director.
It was supposed to be just another Saturday. But in 19.6 seconds, six people lay dying and 13 others were wounded when a gunman opened fire in front of a Safeway supermarket.
The gunman shot Gabby in the head — leaving her with a condition called aphasia. I was shot in the face and in the leg. I was fading and almost died on the ground. But I thought about my family and tried to keep my eyes open until we made it to the trauma center that saved my life.
**Fifteen years later, Gabby and I still carry the scars of that terrible day._Some days are harder than others, but we can never stop fighting._**
Gun violence is a uniquely American crisis. Gun deaths have increased dramatically in the past two decades, becoming more common than car crashes. Far too often, we see disturbing new reports of politically motivated gun violence when we turn on the TV.
We have the tools to fix this epidemic, but we need our elected leaders to have the courage to take on the gun lobby and defend our democracy.

STANDING ROOM ONLY.

I want to take you inside that Minneapolis courtroom on November 16,
the day of my first court appearance, because the ten minutes I spent
in there told me more about this case than ten weeks of headlines.
STAND WITH ME NOW.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

The room was small, and it was packed. People lined the walls and
spilled out the open door into the lobby, and Cam Higby and I had to
stand against the very back wall. It looked like the waiting room of a
bus depot: reporters on tablets, a few patriots in “Don't Tread on
Me” gear, people in wheelchairs, and the families of men in orange
jumpsuits waiting behind the glass for their own turn.

A woman standing near us held up her iPhone to record Cam, but she
wasn't very good at it, and the whole time we could hear the little
record button clicking on and off.

“There is no recording in this courtroom,” the judge said, looking
out over the room. Then, to someone else: “Take your hat off.”

I kept my arms folded the entire time, because I wanted everyone in
that room to see that I wasn't even touching my phone. When you're
known as the guy who records everyone, you learn to be careful about
that.

Then the judge looked up from his papers. “IS THIS THE... O'KEEFE
CASE?”

Cam and I made our way up to the front of the room together. HELP ME
KEEP GOING.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Here is what I need you to know about those ten minutes, because the
prosecution had only one real request that day, and it told me
everything. They asked the judge to BAR ME FROM TALKING TO CAM.

Think about that for a second. Cam and I work together, we investigate
together, and we were charged together for the very same reporting,
yet the very first thing the county wanted from that judge was to cut
the line of communication between two working journalists.

THE JUDGE SAID NO.

He said he couldn't do that, and he even noted that two men had
traveled all the way from other parts of the country to be in his
courtroom that day, which he called a good showing.

And the woman who brought these charges? MARY MORIARTY STILL WASN'T IN
THE ROOM. She had sent someone else to stand at the table and ask the
judge for that order on her behalf.

I don't believe for a moment that request was an accident. Nobody
tries to separate two reporters because of something they did back in
August; you try to separate them because of what they might do next.
Keeping us apart, slowing us down and making every single phone call
feel risky is the real goal here. SHOW THEM IT WON'T WORK.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

So here is my answer to them. Cam and I are still talking, my team is
still working, and the next investigation is already being planned,
because I want it out in the field before I walk back into that
courthouse in January.

Keeping my teams in the field between now and January costs real
money, and the county is counting on it running out. HELP ME KEEP THEM
WORKING.

#### From Our Partners
## **[From $1 Million to $26 Million](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/617c1026-bb92-4b04-92c3-884be45404af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
### How $2.03 of Coffee Becomes a $13.99 Bag
* * *
Walk a standard bag of Colombian coffee backward from the grocery shelf to the mountainside, and the economics change dramatically.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/617c1026-bb92-4b04-92c3-884be45404af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Walk into any American grocery store looking for a standard bag of premium Colombian coffee, and you might expect to pay $13.99. **But how did that bag get there?** Rewind its journey, all the way back to the Colombian mountainside.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/170879f3-728d-4e9c-b3ae-e506d059944e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**What happened between those two numbers?** The traditional coffee supply chain includes a laundry list of participants. Along the way, every middleman takes their fee.
Green Coffee Company's built on a different model. We don't simply buy processed beans and slap on a label. And at each step, more value is added to the same coffee.
Our secret is simple: **Vertical integration.** Controlling more of the processes ourselves means there's less margin leak, capturing the full value across the entire supply chain. **[Review the offering->](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/617c1026-bb92-4b04-92c3-884be45404af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And we have the data to prove just how well it works. Green Coffee Company's revenue was $1 million in 2021. In 2025? **We grew to $26 million.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/af4cb8f0-e095-4eda-b7b8-43eb7a8530b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We know investing in coffee can be hard, particularly if you're looking at a cafe concept still hoping to open its first location. **That 's not what this is.** Instead, Green Coffee Company has the infrastructure already in place, with proven sales from the farm to the $13.99-per-bag at the end of the supply chain.
Green Coffee Company is still private, but thanks to a Regulation A offering, individual investors have an opportunity to participate. With a minimum investment of $1,001, shares are currently offered at $1.15.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/617c1026-bb92-4b04-92c3-884be45404af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

#### The Second Count
## **Summer growth is revised to 4.3 percent, and the President calls the first count fake**
_The economy ran hotter than Washington first reported. Now the argument is over who keeps score._
Our partner above tells its story through one growth line. This week the biggest growth line in the country was rewritten, and within a day it had turned into a political fight.
The Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said Wednesday that the economy grew at a 4.3 percent annual rate from July through September, up from the 3.4 percent it first reported in October and [the fastest pace in three years](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e3e06444-d18f-4747-9f98-ab8c345f3312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Most of the change came from business spending on software, much of it tied to the artificial intelligence buildout, plus more consumer spending on goods than the first count caught.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/bddefb47-1af6-4b11-a2d4-80d89cab518a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On Thanksgiving morning, President Trump called the earlier estimate fake and [asked for an immediate investigation](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/786658af-5f80-4602-b10c-aceca3ce9622?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), arguing that it was published before the Nov. 3 midterms on purpose. He offered no evidence. The bureau publishes three estimates of every quarter on a calendar set in advance, and the third look at this one is due Dec. 23.
The fight has a history. In August 2025, the President fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a weak jobs report.
Federal statistics reach the kitchen table in plain ways. They set the yearly Social Security raise, the inflation adjustment on I bonds and TIPS, and the income brackets on a tax return. A 4.3 percent economy also gives the Federal Reserve more room to keep borrowing costs high.
I built supply budgets for two decades on counts that got corrected every month, and a correction was the system doing its job.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c2dc1f9c-282f-440d-8fbf-877453b3b68a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a36d4199-420e-4de7-af23-f619ae1b9571?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Our next partner is about looking younger, and this week the stock market smoothed out some of the lines a rough November left behind._
#### From Our Partners
## **["Wrinkle Filling" Trick To Look Years Younger](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/871fa866-a9f6-4313-9e81-0b0d3e60bd25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
We all want to stay looking young and beautiful. Now, one doctor says he's found the secret.
According to Dr. John Layke -- a husband, father, and Beverly Hills beauty expert -- **the two big signs of aging are the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.** (Especially around the eyes, mouth, cheeks, eyebrows, and forehead.)
Fortunately, this is a problem you can easily solve at home.
Dr. Layke says you can **look and feel years younger, using a simple, do-it-yourself trick.** *
This secret is increasingly popular among Hollywood stars, who lose their jobs if they don't look their best. But you don't have to be a celebrity to enjoy youthful, gorgeous-looking skin with this method.
Dr. Layke has created a short video where he explains his beauty secret from beginning to end (complete with instructions), so you can try it for yourself at home.
The video has since gone viral and received million of views.
If you'd like to **try this 60-second beauty trick at home, you can view the instructional video below.** It's a fascinating presentation, even if you don't have wrinkles.
**[Watch his presentation by clicking here.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/871fa866-a9f6-4313-9e81-0b0d3e60bd25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/871fa866-a9f6-4313-9e81-0b0d3e60bd25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So far, the reviews have been stunning, with thousands of women enjoying a beautiful, new glow radiating from their skin.
One viewer commented: "This is amazing! I'm getting compliments from friends, co-workers, and even strangers! Every woman deserves to feel beautiful."*
**[Watch the presentation here.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/871fa866-a9f6-4313-9e81-0b0d3e60bd25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
*All individuals are unique. Results can and will vary.
#### The Rebound Week
### **Wall Street logs its best week since April 2025, and bond yields climb with it**
Stocks finished the holiday-shortened week with a broad rally in Friday's half-day session. The S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent on the day and closed at 7,297.49.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5e95131d-9fbf-4919-ae16-7ee2ba678b61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* The index gained 5.6 percent for the week, [its best week since April 2025](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8a315ee6-9016-4f37-b25c-68b46484fc00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), while the Nasdaq composite rose 6.7 percent.
* One week earlier, the S&P 500 had finished more than 10 percent below the record it set in October.
* Friday's gains reached all 11 sectors, and about four of every five stocks in the index rose.
* The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.94 percent from 4.85 percent on Wednesday, so borrowing costs moved up along with stock prices.

Sharp rebounds often follow sharp drops, and I would want to see a steadier month before calling the slide finished.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4336586e-df3c-47f1-933c-55fe42a0ddd1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### One Number
**24.00%** is what the average new credit card offer charges this month, the fourth straight monthly rise and [the highest since last November](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fcc5afc5-723c-42e3-a6df-5bb048e6d609?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Carry a $7,000 holiday balance at that rate while paying $250 a month, and it takes about 42 months to clear, with roughly $3,365 going to interest. Paying the statement in full by the due date avoids the charge entirely.
#### Why I Led Here
In the Army we counted every supply shipment twice, once on the dock and again in the warehouse, and the second count was usually the better one. Nobody blamed the clerk whose second count came in higher. The trouble started only when someone wanted the count to come out a certain way.
That is why I put a dry statistics fight on top of a holiday weekend issue. My own plan is modest: I am going to keep reading the official numbers the way I always have, next to the private surveys that track the same things, and trust the pattern over any single release.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6b3d83f2-8e0b-4fe2-9a7d-b7ca816671d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

---|---|---

# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=55%2E6803%2E609ppq)
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261128.ie0BZq&refcode=em20261128-55&t=3&akid=55%2E6803%2E609ppq)
Big Oil wrote big checks to win, and well, they lost.
The oil and gas industry spent at least **$182 million** backing Republicans during this year’s election. Corporate spending hit record-breaking numbers — with **$737 million** spent in the midterms.
Read that again:
**$182 million.**
**$737 million.**
Now compare that to our average online donation this year: **$26.30.**
I’ve always believed that the power of the many can beat the money of the few because I’ve seen it for myself.
This movement — not Big Oil and their million-dollar checks — helped elect over 450 climate leaders since 2022 who are accountable to people, not Exxon and Chevron.
These 450 leaders are reshaping who our government serves, and it’s exactly why JanePAC exists: to back courageous candidates whose morals can’t be bought.
From deep red seats to rural areas, we’re setting our sights to elect true leaders in districts most think are impossible. We've seen that when we invest early in the right candidates, stay bold in our message, and center working people, we can win in _any district._
**[As we prepare for 2027, we need your support right now. We’re setting a November goal of $30,000 to reach before the end of the month. Will you rush a $7.50 donation right now from Cresco to help us reach our goal before midnight on November 30?](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261128.ie0BZq&amount=5&refcode=em20261128-55&t=4&akid=55%2E6803%2E609ppq)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261128.ie0BZq&amount=5&refcode=20261128-55&t=23&akid=55%2E6803%2E609ppq)**
Moments like these bring me back to my childhood. I think of the beautiful birds I used to wake up to in the mornings — birds I no longer hear. I think of the cancers and diseases with names you can barely pronounce, and the lives cut short.
**None of it, not the beauty of our natural world or the health of our loved ones, should be sacrificed for the financial gain of a handful of corporate executives.**
So listen, Big Oil and Big Tech may have lost, but we have seen the lengths they’ll go to still override the will of the voters. I say enough is enough. We need to be prepared for these groups to come back with even more money against our climate champions.
**[Help us reach our $30,000 November goal right now so we can start organizing for the next election. The strong foundation we build _today_ is what will give us the strength to elect even more climate champions nationwide.](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261128.ie0BZq&amount=5&refcode=em20261128-55&t=24&akid=55%2E6803%2E609ppq)**

Thank you for your support,
xx Jane

name: United We Dream
subject: No one hands young people power. We build it.
body:
From Illinois to California, here's a preview of your impact. | | | Peter — we're led by immigrant youth and powered by community. That means this team's contributions do so much for our people-powered movement. As we close out the year, here's just a preview of your impact:
* Thanks to this team's support, more than **70 young people** gathered in Illinois for our **National Member Convening** , where we launched **Powered by Students** , an organizing network for college students. 👩🏽🎓
* **15 immigrant youth leaders** from eight different regions across the country trained for six weeks in **Level Up: The Dream Lab** and then organized and led community events, including training high schoolers, art installations, and even a pickup soccer game. ⚽
* In Los Angeles, one weekend of door-knocking, música, and cultura — from USC to a packed Coffee & Cultura party in South LA — **welcomed Homies Unidos** into our movement family and sparked **new chapters in Orange County and at LA City College**. ☕
* _And so much more!_

This has been a hard year for our communities. Through it all, you've helped us respond, organize, and keep building toward the only real solution to this chaos: a pathway to citizenship. **Now, we're reaching out to humbly ask:** **[Will you make a tax-deductible End-of-Year gift to United We Dream, Peter? clean_body: From Illinois to California, here's a preview of your impact. | | | Peter — we're led by immigrant youth and powered by community. That means this team's contributions do so much for our people-powered movement. As we close out the year, here's just a preview of your impact: Thanks to this team's support, more than 70 young people gathered in Illinois for our National Member Convening , where we launched Powered by Students , an organizing network for college students. 👩🏽🎓 15 immigrant youth leaders from eight different regions across the country trained for six weeks in Level Up: The Dream Lab and then organized and led community events, including training high schoolers, art installations, and even a pickup soccer game. ⚽ In Los Angeles, one weekend of door-knocking, música, and cultura — from USC to a packed Coffee & Cultura party in South LA — welcomed Homies Unidos into our movement family and sparked new chapters in Orange County and at LA City College. ☕ And so much more! This has been a hard year for our communities. Through it all, you've helped us respond, organize, and keep building toward the only real solution to this chaos: a pathway to citizenship. Now, we're reaching out to humbly ask: If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | Thank you for standing with us. In solidarity, United We Dream Follow us on: | | | | |

body:
Help us have the resources to register voters this Giving Tuesday.
#
Peter,
This year, Latino voters reshaped the electoral map, and with your support, we were able to secure huge victories across the nation.
We registered young Latino voters, gave first-time voters the information they needed to cast their ballots, and stayed connected with our community year-round, not just in the weeks before Election Day. **And on November 3rd, Latino voters showed up in force.**
According to our records, you haven’t made a contribution to Voto Latino this year. [**If you’re inspired by our work to turn out Latino voters, now is the perfect time to donate to support our work ahead of 2027.**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20261128-1.d3Lo7P&refcode=em20261128-804&t=2&akid=804%2E1366028%2EMW4G5L)
This Tuesday, December 1st, is Giving Tuesday, a global day of generosity when people come together to support the causes they care about most. **This Giving Tuesday, we’ve set a goal of raising $20,000 to power our voter registration and organizing work heading into 2027.**
There are no off years, Peter. The victories we celebrated this year were built in the years when no one was paying attention, and every year, hundreds of thousands of young Latinos turn 18 and become eligible to vote. So, if we want to keep building Latino political power, we have to reach them now, because no one else will.
This year, on average, it took $26 to register one voter. So now, we’re asking: **[Will you make a donation of $26 or more ahead of Giving Tuesday to help us register the next generation of Latino voters?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/68?c0=em-ms-voto-20261128-1.CQHRRP&refcode=em20261128-804&t=3&akid=804%2E1366028%2EMW4G5L)**
