A pioneer and visionary who served her state and nation as DLCC Board Chair. We honor her accomplishments and legacy as we focus forward with new Democratic power across America’s statehouses. | | |
---
| |
---|---
Peter, The Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee today and always honors the accomplishments and legacy of our Board Chairwoman, New York State Senate Pro Tempore and Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins. As the longest-serving Democratic Majority Leader in New York State Senate history, and the first woman and African American to occupy this role, her tenure is distinguished by significant legislative achievements and a steadfast commitment to addressing the needs of New Yorkers. **Under her leadership, the New York legislature improved millions of lives through landmark policies.** She championed women’s health care and worked to enshrine abortion rights into the New York State Constitution. She secured life-changing funding for her state’s schools, and was unwavering in her efforts for voting reforms, gun safety legislation, LGBTQ+ rights, and other critical issues. As DLCC’s Board Chair since 2019, Leader Stewart-Cousins was committed to building a blue map carrying forward the DLCC’s mission to win Democratic majorities and elevate leaders in state legislative chambers nationwide. **Her enduring legacy rests not only on her own record of public service, but also on the generations of future leaders for whom she paved the way.** We honor the time she shared with us and are endlessly thankful for the lasting impact of her guidance and example. In Reverence, The Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee

STANDING ROOM ONLY.

I want to take you inside that Minneapolis courtroom on November 16,
the day of my first court appearance, because the ten minutes I spent
in there told me more about this case than ten weeks of headlines.
STAND WITH ME NOW.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

The room was small, and it was packed. People lined the walls and
spilled out the open door into the lobby, and Cam Higby and I had to
stand against the very back wall. It looked like the waiting room of a
bus depot: reporters on tablets, a few patriots in “Don't Tread on
Me” gear, people in wheelchairs, and the families of men in orange
jumpsuits waiting behind the glass for their own turn.

A woman standing near us held up her iPhone to record Cam, but she
wasn't very good at it, and the whole time we could hear the little
record button clicking on and off.

“There is no recording in this courtroom,” the judge said, looking
out over the room. Then, to someone else: “Take your hat off.”

I kept my arms folded the entire time, because I wanted everyone in
that room to see that I wasn't even touching my phone. When you're
known as the guy who records everyone, you learn to be careful about
that.

Then the judge looked up from his papers. “IS THIS THE... O'KEEFE
CASE?”

Cam and I made our way up to the front of the room together. HELP ME
KEEP GOING.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Here is what I need you to know about those ten minutes, because the
prosecution had only one real request that day, and it told me
everything. They asked the judge to BAR ME FROM TALKING TO CAM.

Think about that for a second. Cam and I work together, we investigate
together, and we were charged together for the very same reporting,
yet the very first thing the county wanted from that judge was to cut
the line of communication between two working journalists.

THE JUDGE SAID NO.

He said he couldn't do that, and he even noted that two men had
traveled all the way from other parts of the country to be in his
courtroom that day, which he called a good showing.

And the woman who brought these charges? MARY MORIARTY STILL WASN'T IN
THE ROOM. She had sent someone else to stand at the table and ask the
judge for that order on her behalf.

I don't believe for a moment that request was an accident. Nobody
tries to separate two reporters because of something they did back in
August; you try to separate them because of what they might do next.
Keeping us apart, slowing us down and making every single phone call
feel risky is the real goal here. SHOW THEM IT WON'T WORK.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

So here is my answer to them. Cam and I are still talking, my team is
still working, and the next investigation is already being planned,
because I want it out in the field before I walk back into that
courthouse in January.

Keeping my teams in the field between now and January costs real
money, and the county is counting on it running out. HELP ME KEEP THEM
WORKING.

# How to Turn On Incognito Mode on Your iPhone & iPad
Privacy is important when using your iPhone and iPad, and if you're using Chrome, your browsing activities and search history can be tracked. In addition, loved ones can easily pick up your iPhone and gain access to information that you don't want them to see. Thankfully, there's Incognito mode. Learn how to go incognito on your iPhone or iPad in Chrome, and how to turn off private browsing on your iPad and iPhone.
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Learn how to turn Incognito mode on so you can browse for gifts for your loved ones without surprises being spoiled.**
* **Use Incognito mode to log in to multiple accounts at the same time without constantly logging out.**
* **Learn how to turn off private browsing on your iPad and iPhone when you're finished with Incognito mode.**

## How to Turn Incognito Mode On & How to Switch Off Incognito Mode in Chrome
### System Requirements
_This tip works on any iPhone using iOS 12 or later, but it was performed on an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.2. Find out how to update to the[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-17279-262757-8945673-dbc23f607e-7se4375fd4)._
Incognito mode prevents Google's Chrome browser from saving your activity data on your iPhone by prompting Chrome to remove data and cookies related to each browsing session. It also doesn't tell websites when you're browsing privately.
On the other hand, Incognito mode doesn't prevent a website from knowing your identity, and it doesn't stop your visited websites, your school, employer, or your internet service provider from seeing your activity. It also doesn't prevent websites that you've visited from providing ads during an Incognito session.
Before you begin, make sure that the Chrome app for iOS devices is downloaded.
1. Open the**Chrome app**.

---
2. Log in to your Google account, if needed.

4. Tap **New Incognito Tab** in the menu.

---
5. You may be asked to enter your iPhone passcode, or use Face ID to verify your identity.

---
6. You will notice a status message and a short explanation displayed in the main section of the Chrome browser window. There will also be an icon with a hat and a pair of glasses to the left of the address bar, located at the top of the screen. Enter a URL or search term in the address bar.

---
7. To clear an Incognito tab, tap the tab icon with the number in it at the bottom of the screen.

---
8. Tap the **X** to close the window.

---
9. Turn off Incognito mode [the same way you'd close an app](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-17279-262757-8945677-36fcbda6f9-7se4375fd4), by swiping up, then flicking the window off your screen.

---

Now you know how to enable Google Chrome's Incognito mode on your iPhone or iPad, and how to turn off Incognito mode. You can also learn [how to use your iPhone to view open Chrome tabs on your Mac](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-17279-262757-8945678-5be7e1261c-7se4375fd4). Along with searching in Incognito Mode, [doing a reverse image search](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-17279-262757-8945679-a5a5534f38-7se4375fd4) can be useful when browsing on Google.

Dear Patriot, [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckbuO3DAMRb9G7mToYcuaQkWAwXSbNqUhS7RMwHpAkjfYvw-8wXSpUh7ykCBxf32sHxZPTOGnjWCwtbW2lbMvsLVhKhVbTnuu9kDvIa2CCUU5p0Kv1nX8hHWygzez4HrXAxi-PGatueJ8OMy0MTEvoIEtk9IgdzYrNrP58YCJLZsc0Nz7OBeaK8Y4G6dlASmUVPvm5MMrMrGreNthxNTQQ3M5l5JP7OjamGsYTnP0XhqRP4h4EfFq4K4Ko03gcx9djkS8Ttyg9i8aLlv9zYHmGGhM1B22BmhU0LjRkosl8nX1uLZ8VQdEPv-hEqFuJYLHKxL5_B77W3M2FoshEfl8P_bu5NQhdSKf2BoRysZ8faOch2p8-Y3niU0tZGIhWjzvy4f-n3l8GvEnAAD__7w9mlg) My name is James O'Keefe. I'm an undercover journalist, and a prosecutor in Minnesota has charged me with two felonies. The charges are unlawful voting and identity theft. They stem from a hidden-camera report on how Minnesota's voter "vouching" law works. **No oath was signed. No ballot was issued. No vote was cast.** The prosecutor herself said it is "pretty clear" we did not intend to vote. Still, the two counts together carry up to 10 years in prison and $20,000 in fines. On November 16, I stood before a judge in Minneapolis. Since then, people keep asking me, **" James, what happens now?"** So here is where things stand, and the road ahead, with no spin. [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckbuO3DAMRb9G7mToYcuaQkWAwXSbNqUhS7RMwHpAkjfYvw-8wXSpUh7ykCBxf32sHxZPTOGnjWCwtbW2lbMvsLVhKhVbTnuu9kDvIa2CCUU5p0Kv1nX8hHWygzez4HrXAxi-PGatueJ8OMy0MTEvoIEtk9IgdzYrNrP58YCJLZsc0Nz7OBeaK8Y4G6dlASmUVPvm5MMrMrGreNthxNTQQ3M5l5JP7OjamGsYTnP0XhqRP4h4EfFq4K4Ko03gcx9djkS8Ttyg9i8aLlv9zYHmGGhM1B22BmhU0LjRkosl8nX1uLZ8VQdEPv-hEqFuJYLHKxL5_B77W3M2FoshEfl8P_bu5NQhdSKf2BoRysZ8faOch2p8-Y3niU0tZGIhWjzvy4f-n3l8GvEnAAD__7w9mlg) | [STAND WITH JAMES — GIVE TO THE O'KEEFE DEFENSE FUND HOSTED BY LIBERTY GUARD →](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckbuO3DAMRb9G7mToYcuaQkWAwXSbNqUhS7RMwHpAkjfYvw-8wXSpUh7ykCBxf32sHxZPTOGnjWCwtbW2lbMvsLVhKhVbTnuu9kDvIa2CCUU5p0Kv1nX8hHWygzez4HrXAxi-PGatueJ8OMy0MTEvoIEtk9IgdzYrNrP58YCJLZsc0Nz7OBeaK8Y4G6dlASmUVPvm5MMrMrGreNthxNTQQ3M5l5JP7OjamGsYTnP0XhqRP4h4EfFq4K4Ko03gcx9djkS8Ttyg9i8aLlv9zYHmGGhM1B22BmhU0LjRkosl8nX1uLZ8VQdEPv-hEqFuJYLHKxL5_B77W3M2FoshEfl8P_bu5NQhdSKf2BoRysZ8faOch2p8-Y3niU0tZGIhWjzvy4f-n3l8GvEnAAD__7w9mlg)
---
Done: the summons. It ordered me to appear in Minneapolis and warned, in capital letters, that if I didn't, **" a WARRANT FOR YOUR ARREST shall be issued."** I showed up.
---
Done: the first appearance. I stood before a judge in Minneapolis on November 16 while the charges were read. The case is now pending, and I'm due back in court in January.
---
Next: the hearings, starting in January. This is where many cases are won or lost. The law bars misrepresenting your identity "in applying for a ballot." I never asked for a ballot or signed anything. The complaint relies on a state election manual to argue otherwise, and my attorneys can ask the judge to throw these charges out.
---
Then, if it comes to it: trial. If the state won't drop this, we go before a jury, with weeks of preparation and witnesses.
---
[CHIP IN $35 — O'KEEFE DEFENSE FUND HOSTED BY LIBERTY GUARD →](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckbuO3DAMRb9G7mToYcuaQkWAwXSbNqUhS7RMwHpAkjfYvw-8wXSpUh7ykCBxf32sHxZPTOGnjWCwtbW2lbMvsLVhKhVbTnuu9kDvIa2CCUU5p0Kv1nX8hHWygzez4HrXAxi-PGatueJ8OMy0MTEvoIEtk9IgdzYrNrP58YCJLZsc0Nz7OBeaK8Y4G6dlASmUVPvm5MMrMrGreNthxNTQQ3M5l5JP7OjamGsYTnP0XhqRP4h4EfFq4K4Ko03gcx9djkS8Ttyg9i8aLlv9zYHmGGhM1B22BmhU0LjRkosl8nX1uLZ8VQdEPv-hEqFuJYLHKxL5_B77W3M2FoshEfl8P_bu5NQhdSKf2BoRysZ8faOch2p8-Y3niU0tZGIhWjzvy4f-n3l8GvEnAAD__7w9mlg)
---
Every one of those steps costs money.

---|---
02 | **Travel** to every court date.
03 | **Filings and transcripts** , which add up fast.
04 | **Investigators** to go through every frame of footage.
05 | **Trial prep** , if it comes to that.
A full felony defense through trial can run into six figures.
The state doesn't have to worry about any of that, because it has an entire office of prosecutors paid for by taxpayers.
I have you.

I'm not giving up. But I can't pay for this alone.

It ordered me to appear in Minneapolis and warned, in capital letters, that if I didn't, " a WARRANT FOR YOUR ARREST shall be issued." I showed up. Done: the first appearance. I stood before a judge in Minneapolis on November 16 while the charges were read. The case is now pending, and I'm due back in court in January. Next: the hearings, starting in January. This is where many cases are won or lost. The law bars misrepresenting your identity "in applying for a ballot." I never asked for a ballot or signed anything. The complaint relies on a state election manual to argue otherwise, and my attorneys can ask the judge to throw these charges out. Then, if it comes to it: trial. If the state won't drop this, we go before a jury, with weeks of preparation and witnesses. Every one of those steps costs money. 01 | Minnesota defense lawyers who know these courts. ---|--- 02 | Travel to every court date. 03 | Filings and transcripts , which add up fast. 04 | Investigators to go through every frame of footage. 05 | Trial prep , if it comes to that. A full felony defense through trial can run into six figures. The state doesn't have to worry about any of that, because it has an entire office of prosecutors paid for by taxpayers. I have you. Patriot, this is how lawfare works. The government doesn't have to win. It only has to make the fight so long and so expensive that the defendant runs out of money or gives up. I'm not giving up. But I can't pay for this alone. In Truth, James O 'Keefe Founder and CEO O'Keefe Media Group P.S. The state has a whole office of lawyers on the taxpayer's dime. I have you. | Pop Acta Media | Inside Scoop Politics PO Box 2221 Fort Collins, CO 80522 | _

name: Sen. Jeff Bridges
subject: 1.5 million votes and 30,000 miles
body:
We won, and drove more than once around the earth to do it

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/558947df3ea8/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10380589?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18BiIVcuwSW?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
On Election Day, more than 1.5 million Coloradans voted to invest Colorado's dollars in Colorado. We won by more than 20 points.
Over the course of the campaign we drove 30,000 miles—more than the circumference of the planet—and heard from folks across the state who are struggling to afford housing, utility bills, child care, groceries, and more. We heard about what it costs to build a life here, and how that cost just keeps going up.
We went from Alamosa to Adams County, Fort Collins to Fort Morgan, Steamboat to Sterling. And Pueblo. Lots of trips to Pueblo.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/TbtQYOxDDPG?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| |
Taking on our cost of living crisis is why I ran for Treasurer. Even though the office doesn't get many headlines, we can put billions into making our state more affordable. Instead of parking the state's dollars in Wall Street and Washington, I'll put them to work building Colorado. Housing, renewable energy, infrastructure. Colorado dollars for Colorado.
In the Bridges household, we believe a campaign done right is good for the soul. Ours and our democracy's. Thank you to those who have been here since the beginning, and to those just joining the adventure.
I'm grateful to the folks who took the time to talk with us, whether I knocked on their door or they came out to an event, and especially grateful to have my family onstage with me on Election Night. The way we won reflects what we believe.
I'm energized by the challenge to align our state's investments with our values. The transition is underway, and I take office in January. More on the great team we're building coming soon.
We can't wait to get to work!
And I really look forward to the next 30,000 miles.
---
| | Talk soon,
P.S. In full transparency, my incredible campaign manager Michael Stella drove most of those 30,000 miles while I did call time or event prep. He's a champion.

name: Representative Ryan Chamberlin
subject: You paid for your home. You should own it.
body:
I wrote a book about what true home ownership should mean for American families.
| |
---
| Imagine making the last payment on your home. You put the statement down, look around, and say, “We did it. This place is ours.”Think about what went into that moment. Years of setting money aside. Repairs you didn’t plan for. Payments you made when something else needed the money.That’s the American Dream a lot of us were raised to believe in. Work hard, pay for a place of your own, and build something you can leave to your children.I believe that last payment ought to mean something. So here’s the question I want us to wrestle with: What does it mean to own your home when you still owe property taxes on it year after year?I wrote _End Property Tax Now_ to lay out my answer and explain what it would take to change the system. I want you to have the argument in your hands so you can read it for yourself and talk it through with someone you care about.
---

Where I come from, when your community needs somebody to step up, you step up. You don't wait for permission or for someone else to do it. That's why I'm running for Congress. On November 3, voters across this district told me they want a change. Democrats, Republicans, and independents all want someone who will listen and remember who they work for. Now, we're headed to a runoff on December 12. Runoffs are short, fast, and expensive. We have only a few weeks to reach voters again, including many who supported someone else on November 3 and are now looking at this race with fresh eyes. What we raise in the next few days decides how many doors we knock and how many voters we reach in this critical period. **[I need your help to win this runoff. body:
Our fundraising is going dark soon.
# [](https://governorhinojosa.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Usually, you could expect a lot of fundraising requests from a newly-elected public official as they build out their infrastructure and prepare for new attacks from the other side. **But that doesn’t apply to Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa in Texas.**
You won’t receive a single fundraising message from Gina’s campaign from mid-December until late June. The Texas Ethics Commission prohibits statewide officeholders, legislators, and political action committees from raising money during the regular legislative session, which means _our fundraising is going dark._
Meanwhile, potential opponents who aren’t currently in office will be free to raise as much money as they can to bankroll attacks against Gina’s administration in its earliest days. That’s why we’re trying to rally as much support as we can right now.
Peter, what we can raise before December 13 is all we’ll have to fuel this fight until next summer. Gina needs us standing with her before this critical deadline.

Supporting small businesses and startups across Colorado has been important to me for _decades._
After the dot-com bust, I joined a group of leaders who leaned in to support companies that built their businesses in Colorado. I also co-founded Startup Colorado as a way to connect startups all across our state, including in rural areas beyond the Front Range. Later, I co-founded the Bridge Entrepreneurs Network, or BEN Colorado. To date, this network has advised over 400 Colorado companies, and those companies have employed more than 20,000 Coloradans.
It is clear to me, after being active in these spaces, that here in Colorado, we ask “How can I help?” and balance our spirit of independence with a strong tradition of collaboration.
_That sentiment shows up time and time again across our small business communities._ I’m eager to show them support, especially today, so I’m asking:

name: Marlo Oaks
subject: Lunch Invitation: Navigating a Changing Financial Landscape
body:
Join Utah State Treasurer Marlo Oaks & special guest Chris Olson as they discuss todays financial landscape.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/VVGILPRgYTu?e=856394ec00&c2id=bd177a39046ea92cef9409845929775c)
| |
I'm excited to invite you to a fundraising lunch supporting Utah Treasurer Marlo Oaks on at 12PM onThursday, December 10th at Caffe Molise, featuring special guest Chris Olson, Chief Investment Officer of Hatch Cove Capital.
Chris has more than 30 years of experience analyzing companies around the world and has produced the top-performing Diversified Real Assets portfolio track record in the U.S. and U.K. over the past 1-, 3-, and 5-year periods! Chris will discuss the global economic outlook, changes in the financial infrastructure affecting banks, credit unions, and citizens, and portfolio positioning for what's ahead.
In addition to hearing from an accomplished investment professional, this is an opportunity to support Treasurer Oaks, whose leadership has made a significant impact in Utah and nationally. His accomplishments include:
* **Shaping national financial and economic policy.** As he concludes two years as National Chairman of the State Financial Officers Foundation (SFOF), following other leadership roles in 2023 and 2024, Treasurer Oaks has established a national voice on financial and economic policy. Through congressional testimony, national media coverage, and collaboration with policymakers and financial institutions, he has helped shape discussions on economic freedom, investment policy, and financial innovation.

* **Championing banks and credit unions.** As leader of the SFOF National Banking Task Force, he brings together state financial officers, current and former regulators, economists, and industry leaders to address barriers to new bank formation and strengthen community banking. He also works closely with Utah banks and credit unions to understand their challenges and advocate for policies that support their long-term success.

* **Standing up for financial institutions, free markets, and economic freedom.** He has worked closely with banks, credit unions, and financial industry leaders to understand their concerns, identify practical solutions, and address government policies that restrict consumer choice, undermine free markets, and create unnecessary barriers for financial institutions. Through these partnerships, he has helped advance national efforts to challenge environmental, social, and governance (ESG) policies, contributing to changes in financial industry practices and policies both nationally and in Utah.

* **Strengthening investment management and operations.** Drawing on more than 25 years of institutional investment experience, he has strengthened the management of Utah's public investments by expanding professional investment resources and improving oversight of long-term portfolios, while also prioritizing operational efficiency, accountability, and fraud prevention. The results are seen in elevated performance, reporting, and governance.

* **Expanding financial education and opportunity.** Through partnerships with banks, credit unions, and community organizations, he has expanded financial education opportunities for Utahns through programs such as Women in the Money and the Utah Treasurer's Investment Challenge. He also spearheaded the creation of Utah Savers, a voluntary, market-based retirement exchange that helps small businesses offer private retirement plans to their employees.

This will be a great opportunity to impress important clients and support one of the most impactful financial officers in the country.
**Tickets are $500 and you can**[**CLICK HERE TO PURCHASE**](https://us.list-manage.com/5GqnQIGKRxe?e=856394ec00&c2id=bd177a39046ea92cef9409845929775c)
**or RSVP by calling or texting Jordan Giles at(801) 602-7713.**
If you cannot attend, please consider [making a contribution to the Treasurer Oaks Campaign at this link.](https://us.list-manage.com/DVJZxTzceIc?e=856394ec00&c2id=bd177a39046ea92cef9409845929775c) In addition to the accomplishments above, Treasurer Oaks brings an extensive investment management background and professional credentials that distinguish him among currently serving state treasurers.
This is a great opportunity to bring clients, hear from one of the great investing minds of our time, and support one of the most impactful state officers in our history. I hope you can join us!
Team Oaks

There will be at least 23 of us in the next Congress, up from 10 today.
I'm proud to be part of this historic group. Every one of us cares about our communities the way I care about South Texas. We didn't run for a title; we ran because we couldn't sit back and watch home get overlooked. But this isn't the finish line.
We're just getting started.
Come 2027, there will be a brand-new coalition of Blue Dogs in Congress that shows up, listens, and gets real work done for working families. I can't wait to be a part of it.

_Formerly All On The Line_

Have you had a moment to catch your breath, Peter?
It's been a few weeks, so I thought it was time to reflect on the lessons from this election cycle.
If nothing else, I believe the midterms were a testament to the fact that we — the people — have the power to protect democracy when we use that power at the ballot box.
**In spite of relentless attacks on fair elections, in spite of a Supreme Court determined to wipe away decades of progress on voting rights, in spite of politicians determined to scare people away from casting their ballots, the will of the people prevailed in this election.**
That's a victory for those of us who believe in representative democracy.
But like all victories in our system of government, there is no guarantee how long it will last, and that is why we must keep up the fight.
**Progress is not always permanent** — we saw that play out painfully when the Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, the crown jewel of the civil rights movement.
But it matters how we respond after setbacks. After the Courts’ disastrous ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , people across the South refused to be counted out – they flexed their voting muscle and swung outcomes many didn't think were possible.
And it matters how we respond after we win — in that limited window in which we have a chance to push for generational change.
**It's time to go for it.** We need to undo the damage done by radical courts and anti-democracy lawmakers in states across the country. These are fights that aren’t won in one election cycle — just as the civil rights movement wasn't about one march or one protest or one landmark law.
But it's equally true that each one of us must seize the opportunity in front of us and do our part, to paraphrase Dr. King, to bend that arc of the moral universe toward justice.
That’s why we do this work. And I’m so grateful to be doing it alongside people like you, Peter.

**Let's lock arms, march forward, and bend that arc together.**

Friend, This Thanksgiving weekend, let’s honor Native people’s histories and take action for Native people’s rights. As part of the federal government, the U.S. Congress has legal responsibilities to Tribes and Native people — which include respecting Tribes’ sovereignty and treaty rights. By passing the misnamed _Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act_(BAAJA), the Senate just violated those responsibilities. BAAJA was written by the fossil fuel industry to fast-track polluting projects (like data centers and toxic mines) on sacred Native sites and ancestral Native lands. It guts protections for our environment and Tribes while taking away everyday people’s rights, Tribes’ sovereign rights, and even the government’s ability to stop these projects. I’ve been working with Native people in opposition to this awful bill, and I’ll keep pushing against it as it now moves to the U.S. House of Representatives. To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, Today is Native Heritage Day. Native folks have been stewarding this land for many thousands of years before it was ever called the United States. As you know, the history of Thanksgiving has been whitewashed to deny the violent horrors that U.S. settlers and the U.S government have committed against Indigenous people. These horrors are still ongoing. For example, in my state, the University of Michigan is trying to build a data center on top of historic Indigenous sites that could include burial grounds. I’m pushing back. And the U.S. Senate just passed the permitting reform bill known as BAAJA (the mis-named _Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act_), which was written by the fossil fuel industry to take away our rights — including Tribes’ sovereign rights to make decisions about their lands and ancestral homelands. name: Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund
subject: The man I love is facing the fight of his life.
body:
I never imagined I would be writing a letter like this.

I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life.
| | |
---
| | | Dear Fellow Patriot,I never imagined I would be writing a letter like this. I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life.My husband, Officer Brad Lunsford, will soon be back in court defending himself against charges that never should have been brought in the first place.And the legal bills continue to pile up. [**That's why I'm asking you to make a generous contribution to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) today.**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckc2OmzAUhZ_G7IiwDQYWLFIRqkqkqqLRdGndXF-Ip7ZBxqSvXzFtXqDbo-_-fDo_r_oK1tkwfwdPXUyTjptOD_IQrFueZLcJ0IY5PWiysxaFUDnnuWg0YLJP0iVkpjNogGNGHa_bqmnqVhTZo8OmRNNWahKmhVoWAtW9NUVbNUT8Limz3bGPc9Hwuqx4ezIwNSgVlyhVwWXLygIcxXSKtO53ZxFCgu3XtESkEy4-c90jpXVj8szEwMSwEe6RThDILOkgmBgcOTMxMaxgxJ0wn2Sl8vLDf8jCMDnsyett2SMSk_3t8s6EOiJPxu6eyf5yPX8b_4UIfgU7Byb7v5_zRn_pv-rxMvaDvl3e9Setx1Go_Mc5v70Nr8klJArpOPE25C_tLHZm_W2ds5uqWVnMHqz7FEv_2cWzE38CAAD__yFblgo) Brad has spent his entire adult life serving others. He's a proud Army combat veteran. A devoted husband and father. And for more than ten years, he served as a police officer with the Las Cruces Police Department.Then one afternoon everything changed. A robbery suspect attacked Brad's partner and knocked him to the pavement. During the struggle, the suspect gained control of the officer's taser and pointed it directly at him.In a matter of seconds, Brad was forced to make the decision no officer ever wants to make.He fired a single shot. His partner survived and went home to his wife and newborn baby. But our family's nightmare was only beginning.Because more than a year later, Attorney General Raul Torrez charged Brad with manslaughter. **To put New Mexico politics into context for you – Torrez is notoriously anti-cop and his campaign was bankrolled by leftist billionaire George Soros.**_The same George Soros who, for the past decade, has spent tens of millions of dollars installing his hand-picked, police-hating puppets into prosecutors’ offices across America._ What followed was a trial filled with troubling questions and irregularities that ultimately resulted in Brad's conviction – **including a juror who failed to disclose their ties to Black Lives Matter.** Since the trial was overturned, Torrez and his junior Attorney General, R. John Duran II, have doubled down his desire to see my husband behind bars – and will use the full resources of the state government to finish the job.Now we're preparing for the next chapter of this fight.And we can't do it alone.**[That’s why I’m asking you to donate $25, $50, $100, or more to LELDF today.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckc2OmzAUhZ_G7IiwDQYWLFIRqkqkqqLRdGndXF-Ip7ZBxqSvXzFtXqDbo-_-fDo_r_oK1tkwfwdPXUyTjptOD_IQrFueZLcJ0IY5PWiysxaFUDnnuWg0YLJP0iVkpjNogGNGHa_bqmnqVhTZo8OmRNNWahKmhVoWAtW9NUVbNUT8Limz3bGPc9Hwuqx4ezIwNSgVlyhVwWXLygIcxXSKtO53ZxFCgu3XtESkEy4-c90jpXVj8szEwMSwEe6RThDILOkgmBgcOTMxMaxgxJ0wn2Sl8vLDf8jCMDnsyett2SMSk_3t8s6EOiJPxu6eyf5yPX8b_4UIfgU7Byb7v5_zRn_pv-rxMvaDvl3e9Setx1Go_Mc5v70Nr8klJArpOPE25C_tLHZm_W2ds5uqWVnMHqz7FEv_2cWzE38CAAD__yFblgo)** For over 30 years, LELDF has helped wrongly accused and convicted officers, like Brad, clear their names and win back their freedoms. From trials to appeals, and even presidential pardons, LELDF has a long track record of success.But they don’t receive taxpayer funding or grants, and large gifts are few and far between. Instead, LELDF relies on people like you who are sick and tired of progressive prosecutors trying to ruin the lives of good officers with bogus charges and witch-hunts.Brad’s first trial cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. With the games Torrez’s office is playing, we anticipate a second trial will cost even more. But your gift today ensures Brad receives the legal defense he deserves – not only at trial, but during this critical waiting period when Brad’s attorneys work to get the case dismissed.And believe me, they are working hard filing motions and investigating the corruption! [**So, can I count on you to make a generous, tax-deductible donation to LELDF today?**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckc2OmzAUhZ_G7IiwDQYWLFIRqkqkqqLRdGndXF-Ip7ZBxqSvXzFtXqDbo-_-fDo_r_oK1tkwfwdPXUyTjptOD_IQrFueZLcJ0IY5PWiysxaFUDnnuWg0YLJP0iVkpjNogGNGHa_bqmnqVhTZo8OmRNNWahKmhVoWAtW9NUVbNUT8Limz3bGPc9Hwuqx4ezIwNSgVlyhVwWXLygIcxXSKtO53ZxFCgu3XtESkEy4-c90jpXVj8szEwMSwEe6RThDILOkgmBgcOTMxMaxgxJ0wn2Sl8vLDf8jCMDnsyett2SMSk_3t8s6EOiJPxu6eyf5yPX8b_4UIfgU7Byb7v5_zRn_pv-rxMvaDvl3e9Setx1Go_Mc5v70Nr8klJArpOPE25C_tLHZm_W2ds5uqWVnMHqz7FEv_2cWzE38CAAD__yFblgo) Remember, the prosecution has unlimited taxpayer resources. Brad does not. Your gift today could be the difference between a strong defense and the next 11 years in prison.Thank you in advance for standing with my husband and backing the blue.Gratefully,
---
**_Lacy Lunsford_**

name: Sarah McBride
subject: Millennial optimism is back
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Our candidates won by rejecting the false choice between boldness and bridge building.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=4168%2E21716%2E4sR6t0)
**Millennial optimism is back** — because on November 3rd, voters of every background and belief in every corner of this country showed up to say _enough._
Enough of the costs that make the American dream out of reach. Enough of the corruption that plagues our politics. Enough of the cruelty that grows like a cancer in our civic body.
Through an outstretched hand within a voting booth and with open arms toward their fellow Americans, with margins not seen since Watergate, voters elected Democrats to offices that we have not won in over a century.
And in doing so, the American people pulled our country back from the brink and they gave our party another chance.
From Montana to Mississippi, from Texas to the tidewaters of Delaware, our candidates won by rejecting the false choice between boldness and bridge building.
We melded populism and pluralism. We ensured that we exchanged a politics of purity and perfection for one of goodwill and good intentions.
**And we showed that we can welcome more people in without tossing anyone out.**
Right now, I’m more optimistic than ever about our future. And it’s all thanks to grassroots supporters like you: working people across Delaware and the country who have had my back, and the backs of my fellow Democrats, throughout this campaign.
**And I’m going to count on you to continue having my back as we get to work in January.[If you’re with me, will you pitch in $5 or any amount today to help me keep up the fight for a better future?](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261128-1.hq-d-A&refcode=em20261128-4168&amount=5&t=2&akid=4168%2E21716%2E4sR6t0)**

Through an outstretched hand within a voting booth and with open arms toward their fellow Americans, with margins not seen since Watergate, voters elected Democrats to offices that we have not won in over a century. And in doing so, the American people pulled our country back from the brink and they gave our party another chance. From Montana to Mississippi, from Texas to the tidewaters of Delaware, our candidates won by rejecting the false choice between boldness and bridge building. We melded populism and pluralism. We ensured that we exchanged a politics of purity and perfection for one of goodwill and good intentions. And we showed that we can welcome more people in without tossing anyone out. Right now, I’m more optimistic than ever about our future. And it’s all thanks to grassroots supporters like you: working people across Delaware and the country who have had my back, and the backs of my fellow Democrats, throughout this campaign. And I’m going to count on you to continue having my back as we get to work in January. In solidarity, Sarah McBride
